question: Old results stopped reproducing byte for byte. Which results are affected, why, and does any decision rest on bad numbers?
measure: Re-run a stored result into a copy and compare it byte for byte, once with Python's user folder turned off (PYTHONNOUSERSITE=1) and once with it on. A result belongs to the setting under which it reproduces.
outcome: A pip --user install on Aug 2 at 19:03 put MuJoCo 3.11.0 in the user folder, where it silently replaced the project's pinned 3.9.0. 34 result folders came from the wrong simulator. The one decision that mattered was re-made under 3.9.0 with the same outcome.
setup:
MuJoCo is the physics engine that simulates the arm. The project treats every result as evidence only if it can be reproduced bit for bit, and it stores results as immutable files with a hash.

Python looks for packages in the user folder (~/.local) before the project's own conda environment. So a package installed with pip --user wins over the version the environment pins. Setting PYTHONNOUSERSITE=1 turns the user folder off.

The find came by accident. The evaluation code was being made parallel (several rollouts at once, a rollout being one simulated try). To prove that changed nothing, old results were re-run into a copy. The file writer refuses to overwrite a file with different bytes, so any difference fails loudly. Some old results did not match.

A gate is a pre-written pass or fail test that decides whether a policy (the network that drives the arm) is promoted. The saturation gate from experiment 08 promoted the first policy.

parts.title: Which results belong to which simulator?
parts.why: If runs from two physics versions are mixed, comparisons between them are not fair and no check had caught it.
parts.did: Copied each stored result, deleted the derived reports, re-ran under each setting, and let the immutability guard compare the bytes.
parts.conclusion: Everything simulated between Aug 2 19:03 and Aug 3 13:41 used MuJoCo 3.11.0: 34 artifact folders. The two versions differ in the last decimal place at action 1, and after contact that grows to about 2e-2 relative in the joint positions. Training was not affected, because torch was the same version (2.7.1) either way.

parts.title: Does the promotion from experiment 08 survive?
parts.why: The gate that promoted the first policy ran under 3.11 while consuming a 3.9-era preflight that was checked by hash only. The evidence chain mixed two simulators.
parts.did: Pinned 3.9.0, re-captured the correction data (4,818 rows, all 11 sites accepted) and the recovery set (8 rows) under it, and re-ran the whole saturation gate.
parts.conclusion: Same attribution, same winner, byte-identical checkpoint. The promotion stands. The 3.11 gate is kept as history only.

trust.text: The comparison is bitwise, not a tolerance: the guard raises on any differing byte.
The parallel code itself was shown to be neutral: old and new code give identical telemetry under the same MuJoCo.
Nothing was deleted. The 34 folders were moved unmodified to a quarantine folder, and each still verifies against its own hash.
Only what later work depended on was re-run. The research log says the numbers of entries 03 to 07 are still 3.11 numbers.
The three correction-using policies from experiment 08 had been trained on 3.11-era correction data, so they were retrained.

meaning: The project standardized on MuJoCo 3.9.0. The pin is enforced twice: a conda activation hook exports PYTHONNOUSERSITE=1, and the simulator command line refuses to run on any other MuJoCo version. The broader test of the promoted policy (experiment 10) had started under 3.11; its partial outputs were quarantined and it was relaunched from scratch. None of the earlier checks could see the swap, because they hashed inputs and outputs, not the simulator.
lesson: Pin the simulator version in code, not only in a requirements file, and re-run old results bit for bit now and then. That is the only check that catches a silent swap.

next.title: Relaunch the broader evaluation under the pin (experiment 10)
next.why: It was running under 3.11 when the swap was found.

log:
**TL;DR:** A stray pip install silently swapped the physics engine mid-project,
so 34 results came from a different simulator than the rest.

**Problem.** I was speeding up the evaluation code, and to check nothing
changed, I re-ran old results expecting identical bytes. Some didn't match.

*How we know:* the Aug 1 preflight only reproduced with one environment setting,
and everything from Aug 2-3 only reproduced without it. I didn't know which
runs were which, or why.

**Experiment.** Re-run every result into a copy and compare it byte for byte,
under each setting, to sort the runs into two groups and find the cause.

*What we hope to learn:* exactly which experiments are affected, and whether
any decision rests on bad numbers.

**Outcome.** On Aug 2 at 19:03, a `pip install --user` put MuJoCo 3.11 in my
user folder, and Python checks that folder before the project's environment, so
it quietly replaced the pinned 3.9:

- The two versions differ in the last decimal place on step 1, and once the
  jaw touches the cube that grows into a visibly different run. Like two
  calculators that round slightly differently.
- 34 results were affected, covering entries 03-08. None of my checks could
  see it, because they hashed the inputs, not the simulator.

Fix: pinned 3.9.0, turned off the user folder in the environment, and added a
check that refuses to run on any other version. The 34 results went into
quarantine. I re-ran what later work depended on (entry 08's gate: same
result). Entries 03-07 were not re-run, so their numbers are 3.11 numbers.

**Takeaway:** pin your simulator version in code, not just in a requirements
file, and re-run old results bit for bit now and then. That's the only check
that catches this.
